#dyplyr pipeline
```{r}

library(dplyr)
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at)

glimpse(postings)
```

#dyplyr terms
```{r}
select() #Columns. Keep some, drop some, reorder.
#Similar to SELECT

filter() #Rows. Keep the rows where a test is TRUE.
#Similar to WHERE

arrange() #Order. Sort by one or more columns; desc() for largest first.
#Similar to ORDER BY

mutate() #New columns computed from old ones; the row count never changes.
#similar to SELECT ... AS

group_by() + summarize() #One row per group. n() counts, mean() averages; count() is the shortcut.
#Similar to GROUP BY

left_join() #Two tables, one key. Add columns from a second table where the key matches.
#similar to JOIN
```


#dplyr pipeline
```{r}
jobs |>
  dplyr::select(company, location_state, remote, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::filter(remote == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(days_open = as.numeric(as.Date(last_seen_at) - as.Date(posted_at))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(days_open)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(company) |>
  dplyr::summarize(n = dplyr::n(), avg_days = mean(days_open))
```


#Demo
```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date),
                days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at))

jobs


#Q1: which cat is remote friendly
#Find the number of jobs per category
#Then normalize the number of remote jobs per category by dividing by total jobs 

jobs |>
  #I want to move from unit of analysis being a job posting to a category
  dplyr::group_by(category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote)
  )
```
